Subject: Subprocessor inventory + Chile exemption question

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving into procurement review and I need two things to finish our legal checklist: a current subprocessor inventory (names, services, countries) and confirmation whether Redwood relies on any processors that operate from Chile or otherwise route Chilean customer data outside the country.

BlueHarbor has a conditional exemption clause for a subset of telemetry processors; if you rely on any transient analytics/edge partners in Chile we need to understand whether you can commit to an onshore fallback or provide a rollback/takeover plan in case a processor becomes non-compliant.

I've attached our short DPA questionnaire for reference. Can you share the inventory and the proposed rollback steps by end of week? If needed we can schedule a quick call.

Thanks,
Carlos Ramos
Sr. Counsel, BlueHarbor Finance

Subject: Re: Subprocessor inventory + Chile exemption question

Hi Carlos and team,

Thanks for flagging. I reviewed the attached roster and BlueHarbor's questionnaire. Summary and proposed remediation language below.

Summary:
- The two transient analytics processors are vendor names: EdgeSight Ltd. (operates in CL) and TeleDontic (edge CDN analytics, hosted in CL/EU depending on customer routing). Neither stores raw customer payloads beyond short-lived telemetry; both process aggregated/hashed logs and use TLS in transit.
- Both vendors are captured in Redwood's DPA Annex A and have signed our standard subprocessor addendum.

BlueHarbor conditional exemption assessment:
- We believe both vendors meet the limited-exemption criteria in your questionnaire because (a) they only receive trimmed telemetry, (b) we retain control of keys and do not provision customer S3 access, and (c) we can route traffic to an onshore fallback.

Rollback / takeover checklist (proposed 3-step minimal):
1) Immediate routing change (T+1 hour): Re-route requests away from the affected processor to onshore CDN/analytics pool (pre-provisioned). Ops runbook: switch route flag in RouterConfig -> autoscale onshore pool.
2) Data restitution (T+24 hours): Export recent telemetry batch (sha256-hashed) and push to BlueHarbor-controlled S3 bucket; notify BlueHarbor SOC with evidence package.
3) Confirm & certify (T+72 hours): Legal performs a compliance certification and we provide a red-team report verifying no data retention outside allowed bounds; if retention found, we initiate data purge and provide logs.

Attachments: rollback-checklist-20261204.docx (DOCX)

Operational notes (Marissa): Marissa, can you confirm the onshore fallback pool capacity and whether the T+1 steps are fully automated or require manual ops?

Carlos — if that timeline looks tight we can extend the remediation window per contract. I'm attaching a short annex language we can add to the DPA to reflect the rollback SLA.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

If you can update the annex with those two changes we'll push this through procurement. Otherwise a 30-minute call Monday morning to align would work.

Thanks,
Carlos Ramos
